Home/IoT sensors/Pressure sensor

Wireless pressure
sensors.

Know the pressure. See the operating picture.

The Hitelecom H Series wireless pressure sensor measures pressure at a selected liquid or gas process connection and sends readings over 4G, NB-IoT or LoRa, depending on the model. Use it to follow water-service, compressed-air and hydraulic pressure with remote records and configured alerts. Select the measurement range, process interface, reporting profile and platform connection around your installation.

KEY FEATURES

Read the pressure.
See the pattern.

Bring readings from pumps, process lines and equipment utilities into a shared view. Match the sensing assembly and reporting profile to the work your team needs to do.

A range for your process.

Choose from published full-scale options of 1, 1.6, 3.5, 7, 10, 20, 35 and 100 MPa. Specify the normal pressure and highest expected process pressure together.

Measurement you can specify.

Published accuracy is ±0.5% FS, with long-term stability of ±0.2% FS/year. Match the selected span and accuracy to the pressure changes that matter to the project.

Battery-powered monitoring.

The published service-life claim is more than 10 years at one-hour reporting. Define sampling, network conditions, temperature and the maintenance target for the supplied configuration.

IP68 enclosure protection.

A protected wireless housing supports exposed installations. Select the pressure probe, process connection, cable arrangement and enclosure mount for the measurement point.

Wireless that fits the site.

Select the configured 4G, NB-IoT or LoRa variant for your coverage and infrastructure. Agree the radio, network access and reporting profile as one deployment.

A clear path to your platform.

MQTT reporting supports Hitelecom Cloud, customer-cloud or private-platform projects. Agree pressure units, device identification, payload and configured alert rules with your team.

MEASUREMENT & PROCESS CONNECTION

Start with the process.
Specify the pressure point.

A useful pressure record starts with a clear measurement purpose and a suitable process connection. Define what you want to observe, where the pressure is taken and how the assembly will be installed. The probe form and enclosure arrangement can be configured around the project.

01↗

Define the measurement.

Specify the pressure reference, operating range and change you need to observe. Gauge, absolute, differential and low-pressure tasks call for an appropriate sensing arrangement.

Normal and maximum pressure · Required reference · Observation timescale

Share the actual liquid or gas, operating and cleaning temperatures, and the existing thread, flange or sanitary connection. The wetted materials and sealing interface are selected around these conditions.

Select the probe, cable and enclosure form around access, temperature, vibration and radio reception. A pressure-port photo or drawing helps the project team identify a practical connection and protected housing position.

PROBE, CABLE & INSTALLATION

A connection for the process.
A position for the terminal.

Connect the pressure probe through an approved, appropriately rated process port, with isolation or a specialist interface where the project requires it. Secure the wireless enclosure at a suitable position using the selected mount; the enclosure support and the pressure connection have separate roles. The product image shows one probe-and-cable form, with other assemblies considered for the installation.

FROM PRESSURE TO ACTION

Measure. Report.
Keep teams informed.

Set measurement requirements around the pressure behaviour you need to observe. Set reporting around when the team needs remote updates. Agree the supported sampling and transmission profile, configured alert rules and power plan for the selected sensor and deployment.

01

Select the pressure assembly.

Define the medium, pressure reference, span, process connection and installation conditions.

02

SAMPLING, REPORTING & POWERCapture what matters.
Report when it is useful.

Hitelecom publishes more than 10 years of battery life at one-hour reporting. Establish the service target using the supplied model, sampling workload, transmission profile, temperature and signal conditions; agree the operating profile in the quotation.

01Water networks & building water6 applications +

Follow pressure from the supply main to the pump discharge and the point of use. Define the hydraulic zone, installation height and operating state so each reading answers a water-service question.

Water Distribution Networks

See supply pressure by zone.+

Monitor pressure at district inlets, network branches and selected service points. A time-stamped pressure history helps water teams compare daytime demand, night-time operation and the effect of planned valve changes. Associate each sensor with its hydraulic zone and elevation, then review readings alongside pump status and the network records used to investigate supply concerns.

Pressure-monitoring objective
Understand pressure availability across selected supply zones.
Measurement connection
An approved main or branch pressure tapping, connected through a service isolation valve.
Specify for this application
Network pressure envelope, installation elevation, water-contact materials, chamber exposure and reporting schedule.
Discuss this application ↗

Booster Pump Stations

Follow the pressure delivered by the pump station.+

Bring booster discharge pressure into the project dashboard for individual stations or a distributed pump estate. Readings show how delivered pressure changes with demand, pump staging and the selected operating schedule. Where the project needs suction and discharge information, define a measurement point for each side and review the pressure records together with the pump controller data.

Pressure-monitoring objective
Compare delivered pressure through demand and pump-staging changes.
Measurement connection
Approved pressure ports on the suction and discharge manifolds, as required by the project.
Specify for this application
Pump duty, suction and discharge ranges, manifold ports, operating temperature and the required observation interval.
Discuss this application ↗

High-Rise Water Pressure Zones

Keep each water-pressure zone in view.+

Monitor selected domestic-water risers, booster outlets and downstream pressure-reducing valve zones in high-rise buildings. Clear zone and floor identifiers make pressure history useful to facilities teams responding to service enquiries or checking a planned adjustment. Choose representative points within each zone and relate the readings to installation height, supply arrangements and periods of building demand.

Pressure-monitoring objective
Compare water-service pressure between defined building zones.
Measurement connection
A valved tapping on the zone manifold or an approved riser service connection.
Specify for this application
Building height and zones, expected pressure, connection access, potable-water requirements and plant-room coverage.
Discuss this application ↗

Water Treatment & Backwash

Put filtration pressure beside the operating stage.+

Monitor inlet and outlet pressure around selected filters or treatment stages. Readings taken in a defined operating state support comparison between filtration runs and planned backwash cycles. When both sides are instrumented, the project can calculate a pressure difference using matched readings and process context. Name each point by filter train and connection position so the history stays clear.

Pressure-monitoring objective
Compare pressure conditions across filtration runs and backwash cycles.
Measurement connection
Independent approved inlet and outlet pressure tappings on the selected filter train.
Specify for this application
Treatment stage, normal and backwash pressures, wetted materials, matching observation times and maintenance access; required pressure difference and combined measurement uncertainty.
Discuss this application ↗

Monitor discharge pressure at wastewater lift stations and transfer pumps to give maintenance teams a clearer record of each station’s operating conditions. Select a process connection suited to solids, fouling and cleaning access so the measurement point remains practical over the maintenance cycle.

Pressure-monitoring objective
Keep station discharge pressure alongside pump and valve operating records.
Measurement connection
A suitable discharge tapping with the selected diaphragm or process interface and service isolation.
Specify for this application
Effluent properties, solids content, pressure range, process interface, cleaning procedure and station environment.

ANSWERS FOR YOUR PROJECT

Frequently
asked questions.

Practical answers for selecting the measurement, connection, reporting profile and platform integration.

Ask about your project ↗
Which pressure range should I choose for my installation?+

Start with the normal operating pressure, the highest expected process pressure and any pump or valve transients. Published full-scale options are 1, 1.6, 3.5, 7, 10, 20, 35 and 100 MPa. Select a range that covers the process while providing the measurement performance you need around normal operation. Send those operating values with your enquiry so the range and any required pressure protection can be specified together.

Do I need gauge, absolute or differential pressure measurement?+

Gauge pressure compares the process with local atmospheric pressure and is commonly used for water, air and hydraulic supply monitoring. Absolute pressure uses a vacuum reference. Differential pressure measures the difference between two points, such as across a filter. Tell us which reference your process requires, together with the range and application, so the appropriate sensing configuration can be confirmed.

Can I use the sensor with liquids, gases and my existing pressure port?+

Suitability depends on the medium, its temperature, the wetted materials, seals and process connection. Share the liquid or gas, concentration where relevant, working temperature, port thread and available installation space. Hitelecom can then confirm a suitable configuration and connection. For viscous, crystallising or hygiene-sensitive media, include the cleaning method and any diaphragm or sanitary-connection requirement in the specification.

What does ±0.5% FS mean, and how is it different from annual stability?+

FS means full scale. At ±0.5% FS, a 0–1 MPa range corresponds to ±0.005 MPa, while a 0–10 MPa range corresponds to ±0.05 MPa under the stated accuracy conditions. The published ±0.2% FS/year stability describes change over time; it is a separate specification. Compare accuracy, temperature conditions and the selected range against the smallest pressure change that matters to your application.

How should I choose between 4G, NB-IoT and LoRa?+

Choose around coverage at the installed position, update requirements and your network ownership. For 4G or NB-IoT, confirm the operator service, supported bands and SIM arrangement. For LoRa, agree the gateway, protocol and platform path used by the supplied device. A commissioning check at the actual mounting location helps establish a practical reporting profile before wider deployment.

How should I set the sampling and reporting intervals?+

Set sampling around the pressure changes you want to observe, and reporting around when the team needs to act. Share the normal process cycle, required alert timing and access for battery maintenance. The sensing workload, transmission frequency, signal conditions and temperature all affect the power plan. Hitelecom can help match the supported sampling and reporting settings to that operating profile.

What calibration information should I include in the project specification?+

Specify the range, measurement reference, required acceptance tolerance and any certificate or traceability requirement. Set a verification schedule using the process importance, operating conditions, previous results and your quality system. For an existing installation, include recent comparison readings if available. Discuss the required test record and commissioning checks with Hitelecom so documentation can be agreed before delivery.

Can pressure readings and alerts connect to our own platform?+

The published pressure-sensor specification uses MQTT, with reporting to Hitelecom Cloud, a customer cloud or a private platform. Share the destination, broker access requirements, device identifiers, pressure units and required alert rules. Agree the payload and the responsibility for evaluating thresholds, storing history and notifying users so the sensor data fits your existing workflow.
